title: Microsoft Purview DSPM: Copilot Prompt Gallery of built-in Security Copilot prompts
summary: Hold for licensing and access-assignment corrections. Microsoft also documents automatic provisioning for eligible Microsoft 365 E7 customers, and Security Copilot group assignments require role-assignable groups rather than arbitrary security groups. The roadmap facts and the gallery's documented behavior are supported.

claims.quote: Microsoft Purview compliance portal: Copilot Prompt Gallery in Data Security Posture Management

DSPM (classic) has a gallery of built-in Security Copilot prompts that users can customize or run directly.
claims.quote: Data Security Posture Management also offers built-in prompts ... You can customize the built-in prompt or immediately run the prompt directly in Copilot.

claims.claim: DSPM reports on unprotected sensitive data assets and potentially risky user activities.
claims.quote: Use Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) to quickly identify unprotected sensitive data assets and potentially risky user activities in your organization.

claims.claim: The gallery is reached in the Purview portal through DSPM (classic) > Overview > Get started with Security Copilot featured promptbooks > View more in prompt gallery.
claims.quote: select View more in prompt gallery in the Get started with Security Copilot featured promptbooks section on the Overview page.

claims.claim: The five categories are Alerts and policies, Data at risk, Potentially risky users, Potentially suspicious activity, and Sensitive data.
claims.quote: Select built-in Copilot prompts from the following categories: ... Alerts and policies ... Data at risk ... Potentially risky users ... Potentially suspicious activity ... Sensitive data

claims.claim: Risky user investigation is a featured six-prompt promptbook that automatically runs its prompts in order.
claims.quote: This promptbook is a six-prompt sequence ... this promptbook automatically runs the following prompts in order:

claims.claim: Sensitive data protection is a featured six-prompt promptbook that automatically runs its prompts in order.
claims.quote: This promptbook is a sequence of six prompts that helps you identify and protect sensitive data across your organization. ... this promptbook automatically runs the following prompts in order:

claims.claim: Insights come from scanned data across DLP, Information Protection and Insider Risk Management.
claims.quote: Data security insights come from scanned data across Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Information Protection, and Insider Risk Management solutions in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Eligible, onboarded Microsoft 365 E5 customers receive automatically provisioned default Security Copilot capacity.
claims.quote: For eligible and onboarded Microsoft 365 E5 customers, Security Copilot is auto provisioned with a default capacity.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter
claims.claim: Customers other than eligible Microsoft 365 E5 customers must provision SCUs.
claims.quote: Default Security Copilot Capacity is the automatically created inclusion capacity that appears in your tenant when Security Copilot inclusion is enabled through Microsoft 365 E5 and E7.
claims.fix: Replace the E5-versus-others sentence in licensing.notes and Cost and licensing with: 'Eligible Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 customers whose tenants have been enabled receive automatically provisioned Security Copilot capacity; customers without Security Copilot inclusion must provision SCUs.' The capacity page's introduction still says non-E5 customers must purchase SCUs, but its capacity section includes E7; cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/security/auto-provisioning-security-copilot, which explicitly confirms automatic provisioning for E5 and E7.

claims.quote: Provisioned capacity is billed by the hour while the overage capacity is billed on usage.

claims.claim: Overage consumption is billed to one decimal place.
claims.quote: For overage units, SCUs are billed up to one decimal increments for the exact consumed units. Consumed units aren't rounded up to whole numbers.

claims.quote: | Generally available (GA) | Yes |

claims.quote: | Public preview | Yes |

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The gallery is user-opt-in: eligible users choose prompts to run, with no documented separate gallery-enablement switch.
claims.quote: You can customize the built-in prompt or immediately run the prompt directly in Copilot.

claims.claim: No separate UI or API control to show or hide the DSPM prompt gallery is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'DSPM Copilot prompt gallery disable hide setting admin API'; 'site:learn.microsoft.com/purview "prompt gallery" "disable"'. Opened DSPM Copilot and get-started pages; read Purview Copilot overview excerpt. Found general Purview plugin controls, not a gallery switch.

claims.claim: The Purview role-membership path is Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group ... Select Edit ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to a role group and grants the group's roles.
claims.quote: Add-RoleGroupMember ... [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter> ... -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter> ... When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.

claims.claim: Data Security Viewers is a role group associated with the Data Security Viewer role.
claims.quote: Data Security Viewers role group and Data Security Viewer role

claims.claim: The documented Purview role-group membership procedure requires the Role management role.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role.

claims.claim: Security Copilot role assignment is reached through Home menu > Owner > Role assignment > Add members.
claims.quote: Select the ... home menu. ... Select Role assignment > Add members.

claims.claim: No API for assigning Security Copilot platform owner or contributor access is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Security Copilot" "role assignment" "API"'; 'site:learn.microsoft.com/copilot/security API manage role assignments plugin settings logging audit Microsoft Purview'. Opened authentication and navigation pages; found portal assignment, not a platform-role assignment API.

claims.claim: Recommended Microsoft Security roles is the default contributor assignment for new instances.
claims.quote: The assignment of the recommended Microsoft security roles to Copilot is the default for new Security Copilot instances.

claims.claim: Security Copilot uses on-behalf-of authentication.
claims.quote: Copilot uses on-behalf-of authentication to access security-related data through active Microsoft plugins.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk

claims.quote: Security Copilot doesn't go beyond the access you have ... Each Microsoft plugin has its own role requirements that remain in effect to access the plugin's service and its data.

claims.claim: Security Copilot platform roles themselves grant no security-data access, so the applicable Purview role is separately required.

claims.claim: Documentation does not say the promptbooks apply policy changes or DLP rules.
claims.quote: Searched: '"DSPM" "promptbooks" "apply" "policy"'. Opened DSPM Copilot; read deployment step-4 excerpts. Promptbook text says 'It suggests recommended policy changes and data loss prevention rules'; policy creation is described separately as an admin action.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, Security Copilot role assignment bullet
claims.claim: Administrators can replace Everyone contributor access with named security groups without a qualification on the group type.
claims.quote: Security Copilot only supports assigning permissions to Role-assignable groups.
claims.fix: Replace 'replace it with the recommended roles or named security groups' with 'replace it with the recommended roles or named role-assignable security groups' in Governance guidance. The cited authentication page requires role-assignable groups.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed because DSPM licensing combines with SCU-metered Security Copilot use.
claims.quote: Depending on your scenario and licenses, you might need to provision or purchase SCUs to use Security Copilot. ... You consume SCUs ... Running embedded Security Copilot experiences

claims.quote: Was <upn> involved in any potential sensitive data exfiltration ... Are there any alerts associated with <upn> in the last <duration> days, and what is the user's current risk level?

claims.claim: The Sensitive data protection promptbook suggests recommended policy changes and DLP rules.
